path: Hero sections, one per design movement. Each is originated within a public design idiom rather than re-implemented from any particular work, so nothing here is built from a capture and no shortlist or spec applies: the credits are empty and original is true. Styles that depend on blur, glow, or drop shadow are translated into Picagram's screens rather than granted an exception to STYLE.md. Nothing fetches from the network, nothing adds a dependency, every random number comes from the seed, and every default already looks finished on the dark ground and the light one.

components.title: Swiss Hero
components.brief: The International Typographic Style: a strict column grid, flush left ragged right setting, generous white space, and information ordered by size alone rather than by decoration. Build the grid as a real CSS grid of 12 columns and let the headline span an asymmetric span of it, never centred. Rules are hairlines in muted and they align to the grid, never floating. One accent, used once. A small mono metadata block sits in a column of its own, tracked and uppercase. Compose grid-paper behind it if you want the grid visible, at a low strength. It is wrong if anything is centred, if a second accent appears, or if the white space is filled. Declare the facets static and text, and let meta.palette list fg, muted, and accent. components.title: Minimal Hero
components.brief: One idea, set large, over an almost empty ground. The discipline is subtraction: a headline, at most one line of subhead, one call to action, and nothing else. No background component, no rules, no ornament. The only tension comes from scale and from where the block sits in the frame, which should be off centre on the vertical. Everything inherits the page's type. It is wrong if it carries a second visual element of any kind, or if it fills more than a third of the frame. components.title: Brutalist Hero
components.brief: Neo-brutalism: raw structure shown rather than hidden. Everything sits in a visible box with a thick border, boxes overlap and collide rather than aligning politely, and type is set flush and heavy with tight leading. Borders are two to four pixels, never hairlines, and corners stay square. Labels are mono, uppercase, and unapologetic. The accent is used as a flat fill behind a whole block, not as a tint. It is wrong if it looks tidy: at least two blocks must overlap, and at least one must break the grid. It is also wrong if any border is soft or any corner is rounded. components.title: Maximalist Hero
components.brief: More is more: layered pattern, competing type sizes, and a frame packed to its edges, held together only by the two tone palette. Compose two background fields at once, such as a pattern and a dithered field, at different scales so they beat against each other. Type sits in three distinct sizes with blocks rotated a degree or two off axis. components.title: Pixel Art Hero
components.brief: Everything on a coarse pixel lattice: type, rules, and field all snapped to the same cell size, so the whole hero reads as one low resolution screen. Use the block glyphs in lib/blocks.ts and the grid in lib/glyph-grid.ts, and draw the headline through block-banner's five row pixel font approach rather than by scaling a web font. Nothing may sit off the lattice, including the call to action's border. A slow seeded shimmer moves through the field behind the type, one cell at a time, never smoothly. components.title: Y2K Hero
components.brief: The turn of the millennium: chrome, bevels, starbursts, and a centred layout with too much going on. Chrome is the problem to solve, because it is normally a gradient with a blur. Build it instead as a hard banded tone ramp through the ordered screen in lib/dither.ts, light at the top, dark through the middle, light again at the bottom, with no smooth transition anywhere. Bevels are two flat tone steps, not shadows. A seeded starburst or two sits behind the type. The layout is centred, which every other hero here avoids, and that is the point. components.title: Cyberpunk Hero
components.brief: A terminal that has been running too long: scanlines over everything, type that tears sideways in short bursts, and mono metadata stacked in the corners like a readout. Compose scanlines and glitch-text rather than reimplementing either. The glitch is occasional and brief, seconds apart, never constant, because constant glitch reads as broken rather than as atmosphere. Keep the accent for one readout figure and leave the rest fg on ground. Corner blocks carry fake but plausible telemetry in tabular figures. It is wrong if the type is unreadable at any moment, and wrong if neon or glow appears, which STYLE.md forbids: the mood comes from scanlines and tearing alone. components.title: Surrealist Hero
components.brief: Familiar parts in impossible relations: a horizon that does not meet itself, a shape that casts the wrong silhouette, type that continues past the edge of the thing containing it. Build it from primitives the library already draws, arranged so the geometry cannot be resolved, rather than from any depicted object. A dithered field provides the ground and a second element contradicts it. Motion is very slow, so the contradiction is noticed rather than announced. It is wrong if it merely looks abstract: a viewer must be able to name what is impossible about it. Declare the facets animated, text, and background, and let meta.palette list fg, muted, and accent. components.title: Sketch Hero
components.brief: A concept still being drawn: hatched fills, construction lines left visible, and annotations in a hand that is clearly working rather than presenting. components.title: Glass Hero
components.brief: This style is built on blur and soft shadow, which STYLE.md forbids outright: no glow, no bloom, no blur, no drop shadow, no neon, one pixel lines and square corners. Do not ask for an exception and do not fake one with a gradient that reads as a shadow. Translate the effect into Picagram's own grammar instead, using the ordered and blue noise screens in lib/dither.ts and lib/dither-mask.ts. A screened tone step reads as depth where a blur would, and it is the honest version of this look here. Glassmorphism: a panel that appears to float over a field, letting it through while separating it from what sits on top. Build the panel as a Bayer screened translucency, meaning the field behind it still draws through the panel but at a reduced screen density, so it reads as frosted while remaining made of dots. The panel's edge is a single hairline, brighter along the top and left. A background field drifts behind it so the translucency is visible in motion. It is wrong if the panel is a flat fill, because then nothing is showing through. Declare the facets animated, text, and background, and let meta.palette list fg, muted, accent, and bg. components.title: Liquid Glass Hero

A thick refractive slab over content, in the manner of a lens rather than a frosted sheet: what lies behind it is displaced rather than blurred, most strongly near the slab's curved edge and not at all through its centre. Displace the sampled field by an offset that grows toward the edge, the same idea caustic-field uses for refraction, then screen the result. A bright specular rim runs along one edge, drawn as a hairline of two tone steps, never a glow. The slab drifts slowly so the displacement is legible as movement. It is wrong if the effect reads as blur rather than as bending, which is the whole difference between this and glass-hero. components.brief: Nineteenth century printing: a heavy ruled border with corner ornaments, centred stacked type in many sizes, and rules between every line of the stack, like a playbill. Ornaments are built from the box drawing and geometric glyphs in lib/blocks.ts, never from any image or icon font, and never by setting a display face, which components may not do. The stack alternates size and weight line by line, which is what makes it read as a playbill rather than as a modern centred hero. Rules are doubled at the border and single between lines. It is wrong if it reads as tidy and even, because the style is deliberately uneven in size while symmetrical in placement.
